metadata.title: Why an AI Can Change a Word You Chose on Purpose.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: why an AI editor changes words it was never asked to touch. Lands the carry-out that the failure is authority, not taste.
metadata.anchor_pair: S03 -> S12 (must be the SAME composition)
metadata.one_flag: S11 — the only hedge in the reel

beats.narration_text: Someone asked why an AI editor changes words it was never asked to touch. The answer isn't what you'd guess. Liam. Take them through it.

shot.new_visual_element: Shannon puppet, lab, speaks to camera, hands off

beats.note: Audio baked into media/B00.mp4 by Seedance (voice MARCUS). No mp3 for this beat.

beats.narration_text: Ask an AI to fix one typo in your résumé, and it can quietly change a word you chose on purpose.

shot.new_visual_element: Résumé line, one word silently swaps

production_viz.label: Résumé line, one word silently swaps
production_viz.mechanic: A résumé line on cream. A single word silently swaps to a synonym — no flash, no highlight, no announcement. The quietness IS the point.

beats.narration_text: Not because the new word is worse — often it's fine — but because nothing in the system was stopping it.

production_viz.label: Two acceptable words; no gate
production_viz.mechanic: The two words side by side, weighed on a balance that stays perfectly level. Neither side wins. Then the balance itself dissolves — there was never a gate.

beats.narration_text: Hold on to one line: led a team of six. You picked led. You meant led.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — 'led a team of six'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — 'led a team of six'
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. The résumé line 'led a team of six' set in serif on cream, the word 'led' in terracotta. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS AT S12 — same words, same layout, same position.

beats.narration_text: The obvious explanation is that the model judged your word and preferred its own — a taste problem, fixable by telling it to change nothing else.

production_viz.label: Taste model — the wrong explanation
production_viz.mechanic: A pair of scales: your word on one side, the model's on the other, model's side dipping. Beneath, an instruction card reading 'change nothing else' being written.

beats.narration_text: But it does this even when told not to, and — the part that gives it away — it does this when its version is more correct than yours.

shot.new_visual_element: Told not to; corrects a quote to something TRUE

production_viz.label: Told not to; corrects a quote to something TRUE
production_viz.mechanic: The 'change nothing else' card is applied; a word changes anyway. Then a quoted line has a factual detail 'corrected' to something true — and the quotation marks around it flash terracotta.

beats.narration_text: If taste were the problem, a truer word would be a better outcome; when the text is fixed, it's still wrong.

production_viz.label: True, and still wrong
production_viz.mechanic: The true correction sits alone, ticked as accurate — then the whole panel is struck through terracotta. Accurate and unauthorized at once.

beats.narration_text: Here's why: these models have no copy button.

production_viz.label: No copy button
production_viz.mechanic: A copy icon draws itself, then is struck out. Nothing replaces it — the absence is the beat.

beats.narration_text: When you ask for the whole paragraph back, every untouched word is re-predicted, one at a time, from scratch.

shot.new_visual_element: The paragraph is re-predicted, not copied

production_viz.label: The paragraph is re-predicted, not copied
production_viz.mechanic: A paragraph dissolves into individual tokens and rebuilds left to right, each word re-chosen. Untouched words rebuild too — that is the reveal.

beats.narration_text: Each of those predictions usually lands on your original word — usually is not always, and a paragraph is hundreds of chances.

production_viz.label: Usually, times hundreds
production_viz.mechanic: A per-word probability reading just under 1.0, multiplying down the length of a paragraph; a running product falls visibly as the count rises.

beats.narration_text: Watermarking can add a second push, nudging the model toward a marked subset of words at every step.

production_viz.label: A thumb on the scale
production_viz.mechanic: At one fork, a subset of candidate words is marked; a thumb presses the scale toward the marked side. Your word sits on the unmarked side.

beats.narration_text: One flag — whether a given watermark does that depends on its design, and some are built to leave the odds untouched; this is the seam where it depends is doing real work.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ONE FLAG — two watermark designs

production_viz.label: THE ONE FLAG — two watermark designs
production_viz.mechanic: Two watermark designs side by side: the left visibly tilts the odds; the right leaves the distribution flat. A single terracotta FLAG marker sits over the beat — the reel's only hedge, and it is labelled as one.

beats.narration_text: Which is how led a team of six comes back as managed a team of six — not a correction, not an improvement, just a word you didn't choose.

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — 'led' becomes 'managed'
production_viz.mechanic: THE S03 COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical. Only 'led' morphs to 'managed'. No tick, no cross — nothing marks it as better or worse, because it is neither.

beats.narration_text: So text coming back unchanged doesn't prove it was protected — it may have been regenerated and simply landed on your words again.

production_viz.label: Unchanged, and still not protected
production_viz.mechanic: Left half: identical text in and out, ticked. Arrow to the conclusion 'IT WAS PROTECTED' — struck through terracotta.

beats.narration_text: And a changed word doesn't prove the model judged yours worse — it may be drift, or a nudge, neither of which read your writing at all.

production_viz.label: Changed, and no judgment happened
production_viz.mechanic: Right half, mirroring S13: a changed word, ticked. Arrow to 'IT JUDGED YOU' — struck through. Two causes fade in beneath: DRIFT, NUDGE.

beats.narration_text: Which points at the fix: let the model propose edits, and let ordinary software apply them, so untouched text never enters the generator at all.

production_viz.label: Model proposes; software applies
production_viz.mechanic: Split frame: the model emits a small patch card (location, old, new); a deterministic patcher applies it to a source document that never moves. The untouched text is visibly outside the generator's box.

beats.narration_text: The problem isn't that the model picked a worse word. It's that it was allowed to pick a word at all.

props.quote: The problem isn't that the model picked a worse word. It's that it was allowed to pick a word at all.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Take something you wrote and care about, ask for one specific fix, and ask for the answer as a list of changes with locations — not as the rewritten text. Then diff it against your original and count every word that moved. The count is almost never zero, and the words that moved were never named in your request. Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Take something I wrote and care about. Ask for one specific fix — and give me the answer as a list of changes with locations, not as the rewritten text. Then diff it against my original and count every word that moved.

beats.narration_text: Why an AI Can Change a Word You Chose on Purpose. Liam, in for Bear.
